items.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: As a producer for your recordings on Landmark Records... Orrin and I would sit there and talk about the project, what we’re going to do, put it together, get the people together, get times together, songs together.

ctx.x: with Orrin Keepnews and Landmark Records, and secondly your association most recently with the S.F. Jazz Collective.

Orrin – he’s a landmark himself. He’s done so much. An unbelievable book of knowledge. He did so many important things for Monk. He could write a story on how the development of Monk’s music within that time that he was working with him, how it all got stronger and stronger, and how he became this statesman for jazz throughout the world. Orrin is known for his gift of gab. It’s hard to get him to stop talking, once he’s – just like me.

items.title: Bobby Hutcherson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He’s always there. No matter where I play, if he’s around, he will show... So-and-so’s going to play, he doesn’t want to miss it.

ctx.x: Oh, my gosh. He puts the pedal to the metal as soon as he turns the key. Rods and pistons and everything’s flying out the car. “Orrin, Jesus.” “I’m warming it up.” He’s – he never forgets a little – favors. He never forgets. He’s the kind of person that if you do him a favor – if he does you a favor, you do him a favor, he’s very – he never forgets those things. You know what I like about Orrin? He’s always there. No matter where I play, if he’s around, he will show, no matter what his physical condition is. If…
As a producer for your recordings on Landmark Records, how was he – what would you say were the things that distinguished him from other producers working on recording projects?

items.title: Orrin Keepnews — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When I talked to Bobby Hutcherson he said, “Orrin Keepnews, if you do him a favor he’ll remember it. Orrin has this very personal relationship with the musicians.” ... I have been upset about is the circumstances within the last couple of years have been such that, we have really hardly seen the Hut

ctx.x: Into Riverside, or Prestige? He came to your office?

He came in. What happened was, Weinstock had come…our office, I don’t really remember why…we were on West 48th street, and Prestige was on West 50th street. Miles was curious. Where was Weinstock going in the name of them? Really curious when he saw where he was going, so he walked in moments afterwards. So, we got involved in a conversation in which I said…I got it now. We had some recent albums on the wall, including a couple of Randy Weston. I had, no, I look around and saw that Miles was looking at these…
compulsions? These were the people that I was living with! They were doing what they felt they had to do! I’m the same story.
